newsitem.title: ROMANIA: FOCUS-Most East European bourses still in bearish mood.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Most East European bourses still in bearish mood.

text.p: Bearish sentiment again gripped most East European bourses this week, with shares easing in Prague, Warsaw, Ljubliana and Bucharest.
Stocks in Budapest and Zagreb tracked sideways while Bratislava shares bucked the trend in a continued bullish mood.

The Central European Share Index (CESI), which reflects price movements in 73 Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Slovak and Slovenian stocks, fell 3.67 percent in the week to Thursday to close at 1,607.65 points.
PRAGUE
Czech shares continued to plunge throughout the week with the three most heavily capitalised shares -- SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka -- applying most of the downward pressure.
The three issues, which takes 45 percent of the PX50's total capitalisation, fell on average by seven percent. The PX50 index dipped 4.6 percent in the week to Thursday.

Dealers put the decline in the context of bearish sentiment in the region but said that the strength of the downturn in Prague was probably due to high volatility of the Czech crown and profit taking after strong gains earlier in the year.
WARSAW

The Warsaw Stock Exchange fell 1.7 percent this week due to profit-taking after the market rose 30 percent since the beginning of the year. Analysts were not sure whether it would extend the correction next week or start rising again.

Analysts said some blue chips, which were the engine of the two-month growth on the Warsaw exchange, seemed fairly priced, but the overall market, which fell 4.7 percent after the surge, was becoming attractive.
Some analysts also said a recent zloty depreciation was making the Warsaw bourse more attractive for foreign investors.
BUDAPEST

Hungarian share prices were mixed and daily spot share turnover was modest this week as the Budapest bourse received little help from the strong dollar and rising trend on western markets, while domestic factors had hardly any impact.
On Thursday the BUX index closed at 5,459.38 points, down 3.5 points from last Friday's close.

Traders said investors were in a wait-and-see mood, either sitting on shares they had bought earlier this year, or looking forward to new issues, like oil company MOL or pharmaceuticals company Richter.
BRATISLAVA
A bullish mood gathered pace throughout the week on the Bratislava Stock Exchange, even though the SAX index closed on Thursday at 204.64, or 0.52 points below the week's opening.
Brokers said the bourse, which has been on a gradual uptrend for most of 1997 as foreign investors boosted prices, has not overheated and many issues still offered good value.
Steel maker VSZ remained the most liquid listed issue, closing at 725 crowns on Thursday, up 15 for the week.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares fell 4.43 percent this week, as the blue-chip SBI index dropped 63.41 points to 1,367.64.
Health resort operator Terme Catez was the leading faller, tumbling 8.69 percent, while the biggest gainer was brokerage Primofin, jumping 7.5 percent.
Total turnover was 711 million tolars ($4.56 million).
BUCHAREST
Increased local leu currency volatility with foreign exchange market liberalisation affected Bucharest bourse trading this week with most stocks down.
Investors said they expected a stabilisation of the leu, which weakened slightly against the dollar after a rally earlier in the week, which would justify investing again in the bourse.
First-tier Azomures SA fertiliser maker and Oltchim SA chemical plant fell some 6.2 percent and 13.8 respectively to close at 1,530 lei and 1,500.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks were mixed throughout the week with marginal price fluctuations. Traders said the stagnation could last for a while.
Drugs firm Pliva recovered on Thursday, taking most of trading with 6,655 units sold, closing at 465 kuna.

Traders singled out Dalmatinska and Varazdinska Banka for possible future gains amid rumours they might be fully listed on the Zagreb bourse. Dalmatinska ended flat at 485 kuna on Thursday. Varazdinska soared 7,000 kuna to 35,000 on Wednesday.
